activity_context.topic_title: The Area Bounded by a Curve and the Y-Axis

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094530/assets/fb622d0d4c25753001c6f51192a587f3fefed20474333c4564c37f65e5969a89.png)

Find the area of the finite region bounded between the curve $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ and the $y$-axis, as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y & =0 \\ y & =0,\pm \pi ,…\end{aligned}
$$

From the diagram, we see that we want to find the area between the curve $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ and the $y$-axis from $y=0$ to $y=\pi .$ To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡y{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0) \\  & =-(-1)+1 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
